items.title: NO-LOOKAHEAD: information-set audit of the frozen spec

evidence.quote: bars: 1h bars; decision at completed-bar close; fills at the NEXT bar's open (F5-class clock) [LEAD-FROZEN]
warmup: 200 completed 1h bars before the first eligible decision (covers EMA21, ATR14, swing window, and the volatility filter's 100-bar ATR median) [LEAD-FROZEN]

swing level L: fractal definition [LEAD-FROZEN]: a swing HIGH is a bar whose high is the strict maximum of the window [t-5, t+5]; swing LOW symmetric. A level is CONFIRMED 5 bars after its extreme bar (no lookahead). L = the most recently confirmed swing level at decision time; if both a high and a low confirm on the same bar, the one with the larger |extreme − close| wins [LEAD-FROZEN tie-break]
Z: sanitized dry-run on REPLAY_NOT_PROSPECTIVE historical bars (determinism, no-lookahead: every fill's information set <= t)

items.notes: Core clock is clean: every signal input (ATR14_t, EMA9/21_t, swing L confirmed at bar ≤ t via the 5-bar post-extreme confirmation, trailing-100 ATR median) is a function of bars completed at or before decision close t, and both entry and exit (a) fill at t+1 open — the same bar-close→next-open discipline as the stocks F5 clock. Swing confirmation lag is correctly absorbed: a swing extreme at bar j needs bars j+1..j+5 completed, so it is eligible exactly at close j+5; 'most recently confirmed at decision time' never reaches past t. 'Strict maximum' makes the fractal deterministic under ties (no swing confirmed). Warmup 200 ≥ 114 (100 ATR values + 14-bar Wilder seed) covers every stated consumer. Gate Z independently tests information-set ≤ t by mutation on the replay namespace. TWO spec gaps found, neither a lookahead violation but both pre-registration completeness failures because §6 S declares 'THIS plan §2 IS the frozen spec (nothing to freeze separately)': M1 — exit (b) hard stop does not state evaluation timing (intrabar touch vs completed-bar close) or fill price (stop level vs next-bar open), while exit (a) does; the two readings produce different, both-deterministic ledgers; M2 — tie-break '|extreme − close|' does not name the reference bar for close (decision-bar close_t vs the extreme bar's own close). Both must be frozen before GO.

findings.title: Hard-stop exit (b) leaves evaluation timing and fill price unspecified
findings.detail: Exit (a) fully specifies its clock ('at a completed bar close → exit next bar open') but exit (b) 'hard stop: entry ± 1.0 × ATR14_entry (adverse)' does not state whether the stop is evaluated on intrabar price touch (fill at stop level — an intrabar-path assumption the plan's fill model 'next-bar open ± half-spread' does not cover) or at completed-bar close (fill next bar open — consistent with the frozen clock). Both implementations are deterministic, but they produce materially different ledgers. Because §6 S asserts 'THIS plan §2 IS the frozen spec (nothing to freeze separately)', deferring this choice to the I implementation phase contradicts the freeze law and risks an implementation-time parameter choice made without pre-registration.
findings.required_disposition: Freeze the stop evaluation/fill convention in §2 before dispatch (recommended: evaluated at completed-bar closes only, exit at next bar open, same clock as (a) and (c)); or explicitly tag it [LEAD-FROZEN] with the chosen convention.

findings.title: Swing tie-break '|extreme − close|' does not name the reference bar for close
findings.detail: When a swing HIGH and swing LOW confirm on the same bar, the winner is 'the one with the larger |extreme − close|' — but close of which bar: the decision bar's close_t (known at decision time) or the extreme bar's own close (known at confirmation time)? Both are lookahead-clean; they select different levels in general. An implementation-time resolution would again violate the 'nothing to freeze separately' claim.
findings.required_disposition: Name the reference bar in §2 (recommended: decision-time close_t, which also keeps the tie-break inside the decision bar's information set) before dispatch.

findings.title: Weekend rule over-broad: blanket Sat/Sun 'market-closed' can mask genuine Sunday-evening data gaps
findings.detail: XAUUSD spot closes Friday late UTC (~21:00-22:00, DST-dependent) and REOPENS Sunday ~22:00 UTC; intraday providers including EODHD serve Sunday-evening bars. The plan's rule 'Sat/Sun gaps are recorded as market-closed, not data gaps' therefore over-toggles gap detection for part of Sunday: a genuine provider gap in Sunday 22:00-24:00 UTC (and any Friday-evening boundary error) would be misclassified as a benign market property — a fail-open direction for data integrity, exactly what the never-imputed law elsewhere in the plan tries to prevent.
findings.required_disposition: Derive expected-bar hours from a published trading-calendar/hours table (or provider session metadata) frozen at F2, instead of a weekday rule; hours outside the calendar are market-closed, hours inside are gaps and stay UNFILLED_GAP/market-data-blocked.

findings.title: Dashboard integration law internally tense; renderer option touches an ACTIVE co-tenant's code without a stated protocol
findings.detail: §5 declares the dashboard part of PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1's runtime and §7 says 'PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 untouched', yet integration option 1 is a 'minimal renderer-level addition' to that dashboard — a shared-file code change inside a cycle that is LIVE right now (registry: ACTIVE_LIGHT, 2 workers RUNNING; runtime artifacts present in its worktree). The plan's operative protection ('zero writes into PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1's runtime') reads naturally as runtime DATA/ledger, leaving the code-touch path governed by nothing: no named worktree/branch for the renderer edit, no co-tenant health protocol during the edit, no isolation-audit artifact requirement beyond the word 'audited in isolation'. Airtight? Not quite as written.
findings.required_disposition: At dispatch, either (recommended) freeze the standalone overlay window, which touches nothing of the co-tenant, or freeze the renderer option together with an explicit co-tenant code-touch protocol (exact worktree/branch, single landed commit, co-tenant dashboard render check before/after, A7 isolation audit artifact) — and restate that engine, ledger and runtime DATA of PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 are untouchable in either option.

findings.title: Volatility instantiation prong 2 is an expansive (but disclosed) reading; ATR14 definition lacks the [LEAD-FROZEN] tag
findings.detail: 'Enough volatility to be worth trading' minimally means absolute volatility sufficient to clear costs; prong 2 (ATR14 >= 1.25 × trailing-100 median) additionally imposes a relative regime filter that excludes normal-volatility periods that would already clear the 4 bps cost line given prong 1 (0.15%/h ATR vs 4 bps ≈ 0.04% round trip). This narrows observation scope beyond the owner's literal words. It is disclosed as [LEAD-FROZEN], frozen pre-observation, and bounded, so it completes rather than corrupts — but the owner should see it called out. Separately, ATR14 (Wilder, period 14, on 1h) is itself a Lead instantiation presented without the [LEAD-FROZEN] tag, an internal inconsistency in the plan's own tagging convention.
findings.required_disposition: Surface prong 2 to the owner at GO review; add the [LEAD-FROZEN] tag to the ATR14 definition line for tagging-convention consistency.

findings.title: Open-position valuation during feed outage lacks the explicit UNAVAILABLE_FAIL_CLOSED law
findings.detail: Gate E says 'WAITING_DATA if feed down — never FAIL for missing coverage' and the fill law covers missing bars (UNFILLED_GAP, never imputed), but neither states what happens to MARK_TO_MARKET of an OPEN virtual position while the feed is down. The class precedent (PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 §8) requires performance reporting for such intervals to be UNAVAILABLE_FAIL_CLOSED, never computed from a convenient later point. The law is arguably inherited by the §4 'per PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 §2 class' reference, but §2 of that plan is the shadow definition, not the evidence contract.
findings.required_disposition: Add one line to §4: open-position marks during data outages are UNAVAILABLE_FAIL_CLOSED for the affected interval; no backfilled marks.

findings.title: Registration mechanics, worktree/branch and terminal-outcome enumeration omitted from the plan
findings.detail: The precedent plan carries an explicit researchctl register command, worktree/branch, lifecycle and a closed set of terminal outcomes (PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 §12 P0, §12 T — deliberately no SURVIVOR/LIVE_READY outcomes). XAUUSD-SHADOW-V1 names none of these, deferring to dispatch/registry. AGENTS.md requires lane work only in the registry-named worktree/branch and registration only via researchctl; the plan being the pre-registration authority should pin at least the terminal-outcome vocabulary (observation-only class).
findings.required_disposition: Add a P0-style registration block (researchctl register invocation with budget-max 0 and the go phrase) and a terminal-outcome enumeration limited to observation/blocked/techabort classes before registration.

findings.title: New XAUUSD panel not explicitly bound to the class dashboard honesty rules
findings.detail: The integration law constrains only the write boundary and read scope. The class precedent's dashboard rules — no ranking by profit, no celebratory 'winner' labels (§9.2), NOT_RUN/UNAVAILABLE empty states rather than 0 (§9.7), read-only with no order-capable endpoint (§9.8) — are not restated for the new panel. The §4 per-number label partially covers this, but a future renderer edit could add a ranking widget without violating any XAUUSD-plan clause as written.
findings.required_disposition: One sentence in §5: the XAUUSD panel inherits PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 §9.2/§9.7/§9.8 dashboard honesty rules; no ranking, no celebratory labels, no write endpoints.

findings.title: Outcome-exposed ancestry of this observation is not declared
findings.detail: PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 §14 establishes that forward-observed strategies become forbidden outcome-exposed ancestry for future blind discovery ('all future proposals must disclose that their outcomes were observed'). XAUUSD-SHADOW-V1 observes a NEW owner strategy forward but carries no equivalent clause, so a future scored cycle proposing this exact strategy might not disclose the shadow observation as ancestry.
findings.required_disposition: Add one clause: any future scored proposal of this strategy must disclose XAUUSD-SHADOW-V1 as outcome-exposed ancestry.

verdict_statement: XAUUSD-SHADOW-V1 plan pre-registration is AUTHORIZED_WITH_FINDINGS. The plan is faithful to the owner's four verbatim conditions and the internal-shadow reading; shadow law (no orders/credentials, TARGET_INTENT class, REPLAY_NOT_PROSPECTIVE, forward-only, no profitability language) is compliant; the F1 fail-closed source gate is correctly re-measured per channel; the core no-lookahead clock is clean; PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 non-invasiveness is bounded; and governance fit (budget 0/0, GO after A7, light worker with the heavy lock measurably held by STOCKS-SEARCH-V1, S1 sealed, DRAFT unregistered) checks out. Conditions on proceeding: findings M1 (hard-stop clock), M2 (tie-break reference bar), M3 (trading-calendar-derived weekend rule) must be frozen into §2 before dispatch; M4 resolved at dispatch by freezing the standalone overlay or a co-tenant code-touch protocol.
